Historical review: all 39 proposed REMOVE screens were deleted on October 14. These images and links record the pre-removal designs, not active implementation targets.

READ-ONLY AUDIT · 13 OCTOBER 2026 · FIGMA PAGES 24–29

Proposed screen removals

The central problem is a state/test catalog presented as a product screen library. Remove rejected and out-of-scope presentations, consolidate repeated states, and keep the agreed creation/editor workflow.

No Figma screens or application code were changed by this audit.

1055top-level nodes inspected
744coded screen frames
39screen presentations to remove
9screens to defer
601screens to consolidate
89canonical screens to retain

Live top-level inventory and all visible text captured from all 1,055 nodes on Pages 24–29, static source/route/contract walkthrough, and targeted rendered review of six high-risk candidates plus screenshots inspected earlier in the session. This is not a fresh pixel-by-pixel review of every screen, runtime test, provider qualification, or proof of feature completion. Current dirty working tree was read as-is.

REMOVE retires that presentation, not storage/auth/recovery protections. CONSOLIDATE archives duplicate full-screen artifacts after their behavior is retained in shared components/tests and prototype links are rewired. DEFER moves unsupported/deferred work out of the active redesign. REWORK fixes a mismatched fixture rather than deleting the workflow. Recommendations flagged “workflow decision” go beyond already-approved removals.

What does not fit

Rejected concepts survive under different wording and in shared masters

C11/C29/B05 still present draft comparisons; W22 still says Repairing; Save indicator, Draft comparison, Connection status, Sheet and Conversation menu preserve rejected controls. H07/N58 still teach copy comparison. Earlier literal-text cleanup was incomplete.

CONTEXT.md:55 · server/src/routes/projects.routes.ts:49

Separate state machines were turned into separate screens

Queued/running/ready, stale acknowledgements, capability refresh, audio-stream checks, download-started and background completion are largely variants or tests. Keep a compact request/history or field state, not a parallel navigation step.

client/src/features/project-workspace/components/ConversationHistory.tsx:18 · docs/design/product/interaction-contract.md:25

Paid and free flows contradict each other

D09/D10/D12–D14 advertise actual credits, estimates, settlement and checkout while the project is free. K21/N26 invent a Billing destination whose only content says billing is unavailable; K15/N109 show zero-credit receipts.

docs/adr/0023-bounded-free-validation-proposal.md:9 · client/src/App.tsx:187

Deferred image canvas is promoted as ready; real utilities need separate treatment

M10–M12/B06 and H20/N65 expose masking/region editing that was deferred. Remove active docs/nav links too. Background removal and vectorization are real Studio operations: C34 and Image tools need integration/availability correction, not deletion as nonexistent features. Keep ordinary image generation, prompt-based edits and Sketch.

CONTEXT.md:47 · server/src/services/creation-requests/preparation/WorkflowCapabilityCatalog.ts:4 · server/src/services/studio/StudioModelRegistry.ts:144

Page 27 should be a capability reference, not 57 more workflow screens

Its 35 G, 10 R and 12 E scenes duplicate composer/viewer/editor surfaces. Move valid model rules into components and tests. G13/G14/G15 advertise an audio input not exposed by the current Wan workflow profile.

server/src/services/creation-requests/preparation/WorkflowCapabilityCatalog.ts:4 · server/src/services/creation-requests/preparation/ActionPreparationService.ts:44 · server/src/services/video-generation/providers/veoProvider.ts:24

Video-batch examples have no matching current profile

W13/W41/W42/W44/W45 show multiple video slots. The exposed video profiles have maxCount 1; image profiles can support a multi-output fixture. Rework the example instead of dropping stable slot semantics.

server/src/services/creation-requests/preparation/WorkflowCapabilityCatalog.ts:4 · server/src/services/creation-requests/preparation/ActionPreparationService.ts:44 · client/src/features/project-workspace/components/ConversationHistory.tsx:18

Draft/context administration adds unnecessary decisions

C18/C19/C27 make the creator manage branch instructions, summaries and instruction versions. Propose removing these dedicated approval gates. This revises older proposed interactions; it is not a claim that their underlying context data does not exist.

server/src/services/creation-context/CreationContextService.ts:18 · docs/design/workflow/workflow-state-contract.md:79

Retry is burdened with another confirmation screen

W18/W43 add a new review after an explicit retry choice. Propose a single retry action with exact original input retention and a new request identity; preserve cancellation and ownership rules.

client/src/features/project-workspace/components/ConversationHistory.tsx:18 · docs/adr/0023-bounded-free-validation-proposal.md:9 · docs/design/workflow/workflow-state-contract.md:79

Different generations of workspace navigation coexist

Page 25 rail/project-media shells, Page 27 Source navigation with Image/Video divisions, and Page 28 ongoing conversation workspace compete. Use one shell with intentional sidebar modes. Keep the expanded sidebar master 1029:84401; retire the older Source navigation only after consumers move.

CONTEXT.md:5 · client/src/features/project-workspace/ProjectWorkspace.tsx:89

The image toolbar contains disabled video controls

The Image transport variant currently includes play, seek and volume solely to fill the full toolbar. Keep one reusable full-toolbar family with meaningful image actions; do not force video semantics onto a still image or create another floating mini-toolbar.

client/src/features/project-workspace/components/MediaViewer.tsx:47 · docs/design/toolbar-centering-and-sidebar-alignment-2026-10-13.json:1

Account/docs/support are over-expanded into snapshot catalogs

Keep actual sign-in, signup, verification, reset, account, documentation and contact surfaces. Consolidate error/success/mobile/FAQ copies into reusable states; preserve native errors and accessibility behavior. Billing and region-editor pages are separate removals, not generic consolidation.

client/src/App.tsx:199 · client/src/pages/AccountPage.tsx:97 · client/src/pages/ContactSupportPage.tsx:57 · docs/design/product/interaction-contract.md:25

Current code is not fully consistent with the approved redesign

ProjectWorkspace still renders Drafts and redundant headers; PromptComposer has a Highlights toggle, stale Review current phrase, Review request then Generate, and routine save labels. MediaViewer still has a title and two action rows. These are code follow-ups, not reasons to restore rejected designs.

client/src/features/project-workspace/ProjectWorkspace.tsx:89 · client/src/features/project-workspace/components/PromptComposer.tsx:130 · client/src/features/project-workspace/components/MediaViewer.tsx:47

Proposed public pages are not routed yet

PublicPages.tsx contains landing/product/pricing views, but App.tsx still mounts the retained workspace at / and lacks these new public routes. Keep agreed public-page design intent; label implementation gaps and fix broken future links during implementation.

client/src/App.tsx:187 · client/src/features/public-site/PublicPages.tsx:14

Prototype scaffolding must not be mistaken for product navigation

Applied/Return clones and Oxx/menu/Output settings overlay frames are often reaction destinations. Archive duplicates only after rewiring; do not delete nested toolbar sources or leave broken links.

docs/design/toolbar-centering-and-sidebar-alignment-2026-10-13.json:1 · docs/design/product/interaction-contract.md:25

Implementation gaps do not invalidate accepted features

Keep video assembly, trim, captions, audio, export, public sharing, history and Sketch within the agreed scope. Veo extension exists in the retained provider; Recraft, background removal and vectorization exist in Studio. Distinguish retained code from new-workspace qualification and complete end-to-end behavior.

docs/design/workflow/workflow-state-contract.md:218 · client/src/features/project-workspace/ProjectWorkspace.tsx:106 · server/src/services/video-generation/providers/veoProvider.ts:24 · server/src/services/studio/StudioModelRegistry.ts:34 · server/src/services/studio/StudioModelRegistry.ts:144

Empty shells are still indexed as completed scenario evidence

R06/R07/R09/R10/E11 on Page 27 and W28/W21 on Page 28 still occupy canvas space after their defining UI was removed. Remove obsolete index/acceptance references as part of an approved cleanup; do not claim those frames still demonstrate the removed feature.

Documentation / Get started
Choose what you want to make. You can begin with words, an image, a sketch, or footage you already have.
Choose an action
Make an image, generate a video clip, or edit a video. You can also import media or open Sketch. Each is a starting point in its own right.
Review before you generate
Write your direction and check the chosen action, exact inputs, model, settings and destination. A missing input or unavailable setting needs attention before the request can run.
Keep working
Once accepted, the request keeps its own setup. Start another draft or continue an eligible image follow-up while it runs. A completed result does not submit that draft for you.
Keep the result
Open a ready result to inspect it. Download it, share that version, or explicitly use it in another request or video edit.

Documentation / Images
Create and edit images
Make a new image from words, or create a new version of an image you choose.
Make a new image
Choose Make image, write a description, and review the model, shape and number of images. Generate when the draft is saved and ready.
Edit an exact version
Open the image you want, then choose Edit image. The new draft names the exact input version. Write what should change. The original stays available in version history.
Work while it runs
For an eligible single-image request, a follow-up can wait for that exact result. Write ahead if you want. The result fills its waiting input; you still choose when to generate.
Choose from a batch
When a request returns several images, choose a specific ready image as the next input. A preferred or latest label never silently replaces an input already chosen.

Documentation / Video clips
Generate a video clip
Start with a description or animate an image. Review motion, duration and sound before submitting.
Choose your starting point
Make video starts from words. Animate an image uses the exact image version selected in the draft. Available actions depend on the selected model.
Describe the shot
Describe the subject, action, scene and camera movement. Check the supported duration, shape, audio setting and number of outputs. Unavailable choices remain visible until you resolve them.
Follow the request
The accepted request keeps its captured setup. A video submission opens a separate empty draft. Closing the viewer or starting other work does not turn a completed clip into that draft’s input.
Use the clip
Open a ready clip to play it. Download or share that version, or choose Add to video. Playback problems and generation failures have separate recovery actions.

Documentation / Video editor
Assemble and export a video
Arrange exact media versions into a cut, add captions and audio, then export one saved revision.
Make room for evening.
Add your media
Open an empty video edit and choose the clips or images you want. Review the exact version before adding it. New still images start at three seconds; you can change that duration.
Shape the timing
Trim and reorder the visual track. Captions and source audio stay attached to their clip. If a shorter clip leaves timing outside its bounds, repair it before exporting.
Add text and audio
Add manual captions to a clip and position them inside the frame. The editor has one background audio track, anchored to video time. Copy audio keeps the original clip audio; muting is a separate choice.
Export a saved cut
Review the saved revision and export settings. The export captures that revision, so you can keep editing. Closing its panel leaves progress and the ready file reachable from the editor.

Documentation / Imports
Import and organize media
Add files to a project, inspect their versions, and choose explicitly when to use them.
Choose a file
Import an image, clip or audio file from your device. Vidra checks the actual file before it becomes a usable input. A familiar filename extension does not guarantee that its contents are supported.
Let the upload finish
Closing the import panel leaves the upload visible in the library. If the browser no longer has the file bytes, choose the file again rather than assuming an empty retry can recover them.
Use it when you are ready
A saved import joins project media. Use as input creates or updates an explicit draft role; Add to video adds the selected version to a cut. Saving the file alone does neither.
Organize without changing history
Favorite, preferred and hidden are independent choices. Renaming or hiding media does not change captured requests, exact edit sources, or previously shared versions.

Documentation / History and drafts
Conversations, drafts and versions
Keep several edits in progress without losing the requests and results that came before them.
Version 1
Original
Version 2
Warmer light
A conversation records accepted work
Requests, answers and results stay in chronological history. Revising an earlier request creates another request; it does not erase the messages or outputs that followed the original.
A draft is unfinished work
Switch between saved drafts or start another request while work runs. Meaningful work is parked before a deliberate new edit. Empty defaults do not need to become extra saved drafts.
A version identifies a result
A media version is one image, clip or file. Looking at another version changes the viewer. Use it explicitly to change a draft input. Reuse setup copies the original request’s captured inputs and settings.
Keep both sides of a conflict
If another tab saves a different revision, compare the two copies. Keep yours separately, use the saved copy, or combine changes. Both copies remain available until you deliberately discard one.

Documentation / Sketch
Draw with Sketch
Use a drawing and a description to explore a live image, then save the exact preview you choose.
Start with the canvas
Draw, place shapes or add a reference image. Add words to describe the direction you want. Entering Sketch does not automatically start a live preview.
Control the preview
Choose Start preview when ready. Pause when you want to stop live work. Returning to Sketch restores it paused, so opening the page does not quietly resume generation.
Keep the last useful image
If a preview fails, the last successful image remains visible. Reaching the testing limit stops new preview work but still lets you accept the displayed image.
Accept, then choose its use
Accept this image saves the preview currently displayed. A later preview cannot replace that choice. After it is saved, decide separately whether to use it as an input or in a video edit.

Documentation / Models and settings
Choose models and settings
Choose a supported action and model, then review the settings that will be captured with the request.
Choose the action first
Available models are filtered by the action you want to perform. No model or input should be inferred from an unrelated image that happens to be open in the viewer.
Resolve incompatible choices
Changing a model can make an input, shape, duration or audio option unavailable. Review the affected choices before generating. The app does not quietly discard an input to make the request fit.
Know what is saved
Each accepted request keeps its model, settings, inputs and instruction context. An old request remains a record of what was used at that time.
Revisit old work carefully
A model from an earlier request may no longer be available. Reuse setup keeps that fact visible. Choose a current supported model and review any changed settings before submitting again.

Documentation / Sharing
Share and download your work
Share one exact media version or exported file, and keep file transfer separate from generation and rendering.
Create a link
Open the version or export you want to share and create a link. The link is pinned to that saved item. Editing later or preferring another version does not replace the shared content.
Check an uncertain result
If the response is lost while a link is being created or revoked, use Check status. The UI keeps the outcome unconfirmed until the server resolves it.
Turn access off
Turn off the link to revoke public access. A confirmed revoked link shows an unavailable public page. Restoring a trashed project does not automatically republish its links.
Download the file
Download starts a file transfer. The browser or operating system handles where it is saved. A transfer starting is not proof that the file reached your disk.

Documentation / Recovery
Recover interrupted work
Use the recovery action that matches the problem. Drafts, accepted requests, saved files and delivery each have their own state.
Lost the submission response?
Use Check status. The accepted request keeps its original inputs and settings while the app reconciles the result. Do not create a second request just to find out whether the first was accepted.
The result exists but needs saving or adding
Retry saving or adding the existing result. This repair does not generate it again. If its destination is unavailable, look for the owned result in Recovery.
Working offline or in several tabs
You can keep drafting offline when a local copy is available. Reconnecting does not automatically submit it. Conflicts preserve both copies, and an older save response cannot mark newer words saved.
Still needs attention
A recovery deadline does not prove failure or rejection. Keep the request reference and contact support. Authentication loss hides private work until the correct account is restored.

Documentation / Allowance
Understand your testing allowance
Free testing provides bounded access to generation while the product is being validated.
Review availability before you run
Available models, supported settings and testing limits are checked before a request is accepted. Free intake does not reserve paid credits.
When a limit is reached
Generation may be unavailable. Your saved media, editing and downloads remain accessible. Opening another draft does not create more allowance.
Check the final request state
A provider response, a saved output and a usable delivered result are different facts. Usage can remain under reconciliation while those facts are resolved.
Paid work is separate
Paid plans are not available during testing. Any future paid flow needs an explicit offer and cost review. A checkout return alone must not grant new allowance before payment is verified.

Documentation / Models and settings
Improve words without generating media
Ask a question or try a different wording direction while keeping control of your draft.
Choose the words to work on
Select a phrase for alternatives or ask for help with the draft. The current words stay in place while a suggestion is prepared.
Review the suggestion
Read the proposed change before applying it. Suggestions are tied to the draft and context that produced them.
Apply it deliberately
Choose the suggestion you want to use. If the draft changed while the answer was being prepared, review the difference before applying it.
Generate when ready
Changing words is undoable and does not generate media. Check the inputs and settings, then submit the draft explicitly.

Documentation / Images
Select an area to edit
Mark the part of an exact image version that you want the next edit to address.
Choose the source image
Open an image version, then choose Edit a region. The selection belongs to that image and its current dimensions and transform.
Paint the area
Use the brush and eraser to refine the shaded area. Check the selection before choosing Use selection.
Describe the change
The image and its selection appear in the draft as separate explicit roles. Write the change you want and review the selected model.
Recheck after a source change
Changing the base image or crop can invalidate the selection. Review or redraw it before generating; an old selection must not silently move to different pixels.

Vidra
Docs menu
Search
Assemble and export a video
Arrange exact media versions into a cut, add captions and audio, then export one saved revision.
On this page
Add your media
Open an empty video edit and choose the clips or images you want. Review the exact version before adding it. New still images start at three seconds; you can change that duration.
Shape the timing
Trim and reorder the visual track. Captions and source audio stay attached to their clip. If a shorter clip leaves timing outside its bounds, repair it before exporting.
Add text and audio
Add manual captions to a clip and position them inside the frame. The editor has one background audio track, anchored to video time. Copy audio keeps the original clip audio; muting is a separate choice.
Export a saved cut
Review the saved revision and export settings. The export captures that revision, so you can keep editing. Closing its panel leaves progress and the ready file reachable from the editor.

Vidra
Privacy policy
Updated January 13, 2026
On this page
Overview
This Privacy Policy explains how Vidra
(“we”, “us”, “our”)
collects, uses, and shares information when you use
Vidra (the “Service”).
Questions? Contact us at support@vidra.app
.
Information we collect
• Account information: email, display name, auth identifiers.
• Content you submit: prompts, outputs, saved assets. Shared content may be accessible via link.
• Usage and device info: interactions, pages viewed, diagnostic logs, performance metrics.
• Billing information: processed by Stripe. We receive limited metadata; never full card numbers.
• Support communications: email, message content, attachments.
AI processing.
When you use AI features, we send inputs to the relevant AI
provider to process your request and return results.
How we use data
• Provide, maintain, and improve the Service.
• Authenticate you and secure accounts.
• Process payments and prevent fraud.
• Debug issues and measure performance.
• Communicate about updates and support requests.
Sharing
We share information with service providers (hosting, analytics, error monitoring, payment processing) and AI
providers you use through the Service. We may share to comply with law, protect rights/safety, or in connection with a business transfer. We do not sell personal information.
Retention
We retain information as needed to provide the Service and for legitimate business purposes. You can request deletion, subject to legal and operational requirements.
Your choices & rights
• Access and update account information in the Service.
• Request deletion of your account and saved content.
• Opt out of non-essential communications.
• EEA/UK residents may have additional rights (access, correction, portability, objection, restriction).
Security
We use administrative, technical, and physical safeguards. No method is 100% secure, so we cannot guarantee absolute security.
International transfers
We and our service providers may process information in other countries. We take steps to protect it as required by applicable law.
Changes
We may update this policy. Material changes will be communicated as required by law.
Contact
Questions? Email support@vidra.app
.

Docs menu

Assemble and export a video
Arrange exact media versions into a cut, add captions and audio, then export one saved revision.
On this page
Add your media
Open an empty video edit and choose the clips or images you want. Review the exact version before adding it. New still images start at three seconds; you can change that duration.
Shape the timing
Trim and reorder the visual track. Captions and source audio stay attached to their clip. If a shorter clip leaves timing outside its bounds, repair it before exporting.
Add text and audio
Add manual captions to a clip and position them inside the frame. The editor has one background audio track, anchored to video time. Copy audio keeps the original clip audio; muting is a separate choice.
Export a saved cut
Review the saved revision and export settings. The export captures that revision, so you can keep editing. Closing its panel leaves progress and the ready file reachable from the editor.

Make a new image

Choose from a batch

Vidra
Docs menu
Search
Import and organize media
Add files to a project, inspect their versions, and choose explicitly when to use them.
On this page
Choose a file
Import an image, clip or audio file from your device. Vidra checks the actual file before it becomes a usable input. A familiar filename extension does not guarantee that its contents are supported.
Let the upload finish
Closing the import panel leaves the upload visible in the library. If the browser no longer has the file bytes, choose the file again rather than assuming an empty retry can recover them.
Use it when you are ready
A saved import joins project media. Use as input creates or updates an explicit draft role; Add to video adds the selected version to a cut. Saving the file alone does neither.
Organize without changing history
Favorite, preferred and hidden are independent choices. Renaming or hiding media does not change captured requests, exact edit sources, or previously shared versions.

Conversations, drafts and versions
Keep several edits in progress without losing the requests and results that came before them.
On this page
A conversation records accepted work
Requests, answers and results stay in chronological history. Revising an earlier request creates another request; it does not erase the messages or outputs that followed the original.
A draft is unfinished work
Switch between saved drafts or start another request while work runs. Meaningful work is parked before a deliberate new edit. Empty defaults do not need to become extra saved drafts.
A version identifies a result
A media version is one image, clip or file. Looking at another version changes the viewer. Use it explicitly to change a draft input. Reuse setup copies the original request’s captured inputs and settings.
Keep both sides of a conflict
If another tab saves a different revision, compare the two copies. Keep yours separately, use the saved copy, or combine changes. Both copies remain available until you deliberately discard one.

Choose models and settings
Choose a supported action and model, then review the settings that will be captured with the request.
On this page
Choose the action first
Available models are filtered by the action you want to perform. No model or input should be inferred from an unrelated image that happens to be open in the viewer.
Resolve incompatible choices
Changing a model can make an input, shape, duration or audio option unavailable. Review the affected choices before generating. The app does not quietly discard an input to make the request fit.
Know what is saved
Each accepted request keeps its model, settings, inputs and instruction context. An old request remains a record of what was used at that time.
Revisit old work carefully
A model from an earlier request may no longer be available. Reuse setup keeps that fact visible. Choose a current supported model and review any changed settings before submitting again.

Share and download your work
Share one exact media version or exported file, and keep file transfer separate from generation and rendering.
On this page
Create a link
Open the version or export you want to share and create a link. The link is pinned to that saved item. Editing later or preferring another version does not replace the shared content.
Check an uncertain result
If the response is lost while a link is being created or revoked, use Check status. The UI keeps the outcome unconfirmed until the server resolves it.
Turn access off
Turn off the link to revoke public access. A confirmed revoked link shows an unavailable public page. Restoring a trashed project does not automatically republish its links.
Download the file
Download starts a file transfer. The browser or operating system handles where it is saved. A transfer starting is not proof that the file reached your disk.

Docs menu
Search
Recover interrupted work
Use the recovery action that matches the problem. Drafts, accepted requests, saved files and delivery each have their own state.
On this page
Lost the submission response?
Use Check status. The accepted request keeps its original inputs and settings while the app reconciles the result. Do not create a second request just to find out whether the first was accepted.
The result exists but needs saving or adding
Retry saving or adding the existing result. This repair does not generate it again. If its destination is unavailable, look for the owned result in Recovery.
Working offline or in several tabs
You can keep drafting offline when a local copy is available. Reconnecting does not automatically submit it. Conflicts preserve both copies, and an older save response cannot mark newer words saved.
Still needs attention
A recovery deadline does not prove failure or rejection. Keep the request reference and contact support. Authentication loss hides private work until the correct account is restored.

Understand your testing allowance
Free testing provides bounded access to generation while the product is being validated.
On this page
Review availability before you run
Available models, supported settings and testing limits are checked before a request is accepted. Free intake does not reserve paid credits.
When a limit is reached
Generation may be unavailable. Your saved media, editing and downloads remain accessible. Opening another draft does not create more allowance.
Check the final request state
A provider response, a saved output and a usable delivered result are different facts. Usage can remain under reconciliation while those facts are resolved.
Paid work is separate
Paid plans are not available during testing. Any future paid flow needs an explicit offer and cost review. A checkout return alone must not grant new allowance before payment is verified.

Privacy policy
Updated January 13, 2026
Overview
This Privacy Policy explains how Vidra
(“we”, “us”, “our”)
collects, uses, and shares information when you use
Vidra (the “Service”).
Questions? Contact us at support@vidra.app
.
Information we collect
• Account information: email, display name, auth identifiers.
• Content you submit: prompts, outputs, saved assets. Shared content may be accessible via link.
• Usage and device info: interactions, pages viewed, diagnostic logs, performance metrics.
• Billing information: processed by Stripe. We receive limited metadata; never full card numbers.
• Support communications: email, message content, attachments.
AI processing.
When you use AI features, we send inputs to the relevant AI
provider to process your request and return results.
How we use data
• Provide, maintain, and improve the Service.
• Authenticate you and secure accounts.
• Process payments and prevent fraud.
• Debug issues and measure performance.
• Communicate about updates and support requests.
Sharing
We share information with service providers (hosting, analytics, error monitoring, payment processing) and AI
providers you use through the Service. We may share to comply with law, protect rights/safety, or in connection with a business transfer. We do not sell personal information.
Retention
We retain information as needed to provide the Service and for legitimate business purposes. You can request deletion, subject to legal and operational requirements.
Your choices & rights
• Access and update account information in the Service.
• Request deletion of your account and saved content.
• Opt out of non-essential communications.
• EEA/UK residents may have additional rights (access, correction, portability, objection, restriction).
Security
We use administrative, technical, and physical safeguards. No method is 100% secure, so we cannot guarantee absolute security.
International transfers
We and our service providers may process information in other countries. We take steps to protect it as required by applicable law.
Changes
We may update this policy. Material changes will be communicated as required by law.
Contact
Questions? Email support@vidra.app
.

Terms of service
Updated October 10, 2026
Summary
These Terms govern your use of Vidra (the
“Service”). By accessing or using the Service, you agree to these Terms.
Who we are
The Service is provided by Vidra (“we”,
“us”, “our”). Contact:
support@vidra.app
.
Accounts
• You're responsible for activity under your account.
• Provide accurate information and keep credentials secure.
• We may suspend accounts that violate these Terms or applicable law.
Acceptable use
Don't misuse the Service. Don't reverse engineer, disrupt, or overload our systems, and don't use the
Service to generate unlawful, harmful, or infringing content.
Billing
Vidra is free during testing, with a limited allowance. Paid plans and purchases are not available during testing. If paid services are introduced, their prices and terms will be shown before a purchase.
Privacy
Our
Privacy Policy describes how we collect and use information.
Your content
You retain ownership of content you submit. You grant us a limited license to host, store, and process that content to operate and improve the Service.
Disclaimers
The Service is provided “as is” without warranties. AI outputs may be inaccurate; verify results before relying on them.
Limitation of liability
To the maximum extent permitted by law, we will not be liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, or any loss of profits or revenues.
Termination
You may stop using the Service at any time. We may suspend or terminate access if you violate these Terms or if required by law.
Changes
We may update these Terms. Material changes will be communicated. Continued use means you accept the updated
Terms.
Contact
Questions? Email support@vidra.app
.

Recommended retained structure
Keep one creation workspace with empty/ongoing/image/video states; one reusable composer and phrase panel; one viewer; one editor with timeline shown/hidden and conversation/media sidebar modes; one media library/import flow; one project/conversation history surface; Sketch; sharing/public viewing; and core auth/account/docs/support/public pages. Put state permutations in shared components and tests. Keep Page 24 as the canonical library and Page 29 as the full-toolbar source/review, not competing screen designs.
Before applying an approved removal
Reconcile direct user decisions in the older workflow contract, update the shared source variants and linked documentation, migrate consumers, rewire prototype destinations, then archive obsolete frames. Preserve ADR history. Do not remove backend conflict handling, receipt reconciliation, authorization, local retention or output identity because their proposed screen was rejected.
